sources.title: Tuvalu National Adaptation Plan 2025
sources.organization: Government of Tuvalu, Climate Change Department, Ministry of Home Affairs, Climate Change and Environment
sources.temporal_coverage: 2025 national adaptation plan; includes current social-risk assessment and island-specific coastal projections to 2060 and 2100.
sources.methodology: Government plan informed by consultations across six priority sectors and Funafuti and outer islands.
sources.limitations: Social-risk discussion cites Deloitte CIVRA (2024); projections summarize cited modeling rather than new measurements.

sources.title: Tuvalu Climate Security Risk Assessment Profile
sources.organization: United Nations Development Programme, in collaboration with the Government of Tuvalu under the UNDP-IOM Climate Security in the Pacific project
sources.temporal_coverage: Preliminary 2022 climate-security profile; pathways described as provisional and still being finalized.
sources.methodology: UNDP-IOM preliminary high-level climate-security assessment prepared with government collaboration.
sources.limitations: UNDP labels the profile preliminary; its pathways are provisional, not a final assessment or quantified incidence study.

sources.title: Pacific
sources.temporal_coverage: UNCDF programme page reporting three community-grant cycles and local-official training in 2024-2025; page publication date not stated.
sources.methodology: Implementer webpage summarizing community-grant outputs and training reach.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; page provides no independent evaluation of sustained resilience outcomes.

claims.locator: Section 5.5.3, printed p. 45, social cohesion and human security discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The 2025 NAP says climate- and economic-driven migration to Funafuti strains resources and traditional land access, weakening cohesion and raising conflict and civil-unrest risks.
claims.limitations: NAP risk synthesis cites CIVRA 2024; it does not quantify conflict incidence or isolate climate from economic drivers.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: NAP links climate/economic migration and land-access strain in Funafuti to weaker cohesion and heightened conflict risk.

claims.locator: Section 5.5.3, printed p. 46, drought, water security and human-security discussion.
claims.paraphrase: The NAP links long dry spells and inadequate storage to water theft and conflict at distribution points; it reports about 70% of the population lacks adequate storage.
claims.limitations: NAP cites Deloitte CIVRA 2024; the 70% denominator is national and conflict frequency or locality is not quantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: NAP says drought-related storage deficits contribute to water theft and distribution-point conflict.

claims.locator: Section 4.2.4, printed pp. 24-25, island-specific coastal-inundation projections.
claims.paraphrase: By 2060, current 50-year coastal-flood events may recur every 1-5 years in Funafuti, Nui, Nukufetau and Vaitupu.
claims.limitations: NAP summarizes cited 2023-2024 modeling; frequency and exposure vary by island and remain projections, not observed change.

claims.locator: PDF p. 7, preliminary climate-security pathway on migration and social stability.
claims.paraphrase: The preliminary profile says climate pressures can push outer-island residents toward Funafuti, where overcrowding may heighten tensions, while leavers risk loss of place.
claims.limitations: This is a provisional 2022 pathway statement, not a measured estimate of migration or conflict incidence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The preliminary profile warns climate-linked mobility may raise receiving-area tensions and loss-of-place risks.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 7, migration and societal-stability pathway.

claims.locator: PDF p. 8, entry points for climate-security-sensitive action.
claims.paraphrase: The preliminary profile warns that perceived unfair disaster or climate assistance could create grievances and recommends conflict-sensitive planning and aid monitoring.
claims.limitations: A provisional risk and recommendation, not evidence of observed aid-related violence or implemented monitoring.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The profile says perceived unfair aid distribution could create grievances; it recommends conflict-sensitive monitoring.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: PDF p. 8, entry points for climate-security-sensitive action.

claims.locator: Tuvalu paragraphs on community-led adaptation grants and island activities.
claims.paraphrase: UNCDF reports three community-grant cycles invested over $400,000 and benefited over 1,000 people, including drought-resilient storage in Nukulaelae, solar systems in Nukufetau and food-security units in Nanumea.
claims.limitations: UNCDF-reported programme reach and outputs; the page provides no independent outcome evaluation.

claims.paraphrase: UNCDF reports climate-data and public-financial-management training in 2024-2025 reached 31 local officials, 42% women.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported training reach; the page does not assess officials' later use of the skills.

search_audit.query: Tuvalu subnational climate vulnerability islands atoll flooding drought erosion government report 2024 2025
search_audit.outcome: Read the 2025 government NAP with differentiated island flood projections and national drought and water-security material; a separate 2024 government hazards PDF was inaccessible.

search_audit.query: Tuvalu climate conflict security land water resource mobility food water local primary report
search_audit.outcome: The NAP and preliminary UNDP profile explicitly describe conditional migration, land-access, cohesion, water-theft and grievance pathways; the profile marks its pathways provisional and neither source quantifies conflict incidence.

search_audit.query: Tuvalu climate disaster insecurity conflict violence blocks adaptation response project access island report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected source documented insecurity or violence blocking a named adaptation activity; the profile's aid-grievance warning is a conditional risk, not evidence of an FCV constraint on implementation.

search_audit.query: Tuvalu community resilience local island adaptation water drought grants outcomes officials 2024 2025 UN report
search_audit.outcome: UNCDF reports community-grant outputs in Nukulaelae, Nukufetau and Nanumea and training reach among local officials; outputs are implementer-reported, not independently evaluated.

gaps: The NAP's migration, land-access, water-conflict and GBV risk account relies on a cited 2024 CIVRA; inspected material does not quantify observed conflict prevalence or disaggregate affected households by island.
The 2025 NAP summarizes island-specific coastal modeling, but the separate government climate-hazards technical report returned 502 and could not be checked against its underlying exposure estimates.
The UNDP climate-security profile is explicitly preliminary and provisional; no final comprehensive profile or local validation was inspected.
UNCDF reports local grants, reach and training, but no independent evaluation establishes durable outcomes or whether conflict sensitivity shaped allocation.
